title: Truth, lived again
hook: truth in speech and truth in conduct

segments.voice: Yesterday, prem: the heron looks holy, but only those who have loved have found the Lord. Your line was those who loved, found.

On my way. A text, sent from a couch, shoes still off. Nobody would call it a lie, exactly. Nothing in it is false in a way a court would care about. And yet something in it isn't true. The words point one direction and the person points another. This path has met sat, truth, many times: in the Mool Mantar, in the Mundavani's plate, in the Japji's opening. Today the Gurus press on the gap between the message and the couch. Truth, lived again.
screen: `ON MY WAY.` → `SENT FROM THE COUCH.` → `TRUTH, LIVED AGAIN.`

segments.voice: First, the ladder, a line you met early on this path and worth climbing again. In Sri Raag, Guru Nanak says: sachahu orai sabh ko, upar sach aachaar. In paraphrase: truth is higher than everything; higher still is truthful living. Truth is at the top, and the Guru puts one more rung above it. Not a truer idea. A truer life. Aachaar is conduct, the way a person actually behaves. Second, how truth is known. In Asa di Var, Guru Nanak gives a list, in paraphrase: one is known as true only when the truth is in the heart; then the filth of falsehood leaves, and the body is washed clean. The list goes on: loving the truth, taking true teaching, compassion to living beings, and giving. Truth here isn't only accurate words. It's a heart and a set of habits. Third, the two kinds side by side. Truth in speech: not saying what isn't so. Truth in conduct: being what you say. On my way, sent from the couch, barely scrapes past the first and fails the second. And plenty of sentences that aren't lies at all still fail the second: I'll pray for you, never prayed. Let's get coffee, never meant. Fourth, small promises. The Guru's ladder makes the smallest promise matter. A truthful life isn't built from grand vows. It's built from returning the call you said you'd return, showing up at the time you named. Each kept promise is a rung on that ladder.
screen: `TRUTH IS HIGH; TRUTHFUL LIVING IS HIGHER.` · `KNOWN TRUE WHEN THE HEART IS TRUE.` · `TRUE WORDS, AND A TRUE LIFE.` · `SMALL PROMISES ARE RUNGS.` · then, large: `UPAR SACH AACHAAR.`

segments.voice: Look back over the last few days for one small thing you said you'd do and haven't: a message to answer, a book to return, a call to make. Don't scold yourself; just find it, and on each breath picture actually doing it. If nothing comes, rest on the line itself: upar sach aachaar.
Truth. Sat, which the Gurus honor in speech and, higher still, in conduct: sach aachaar, a life that matches its words. Today's word.
Your line: truth in conduct. A life that matches its words, one kept promise at a time. That's day thirteen ninety-nine.

howItsDone: Sikhs hold truthful living, sach aachaar, as central to the path, and the line 'truth is high, but higher still is truthful living' from Sri Raag is quoted in Sikh teaching.

chat.says: If I never actually tell a lie, aren't I a truthful person?
options: Not quite. Guru Nanak ranks truthful living higher: being what you say, keeping promises.
Yes. In the Granth, truth means only saying nothing false; conduct is separate.
Mostly. Small broken promises don't count, as long as nothing said was false.
